install_startup.reason: App boots and serves its landing/signup/login pages (confirmed live, screens rendered), but its signup and login routes hard-require env.DB (a Cloudflare D1 database binding via the @aswincloud/auth/d1 package - not a plain SQL connection string, so it can't be swapped for a local Postgres/SQLite without rewriting the app's own auth package) AND a real RESEND_API_KEY (a third-party transactional-email account for its OTP email-verification signup flow). TOKEN_SECRET is just a random string we can generate ourselves, but a Resend account credential is a genuine external dependency this pipeline has no way to provision - not a sandbox network restriction (nothing here is being blocked by egress policy) and not fixable by a recipe change, so left honestly as BLOCKED_EXTERNAL_DEPENDENCY rather than forced by bypassing the app's own auth checks.
install_startup.recipe_modification_note: No Dockerfile in the repo at all (a small Next.js project built for Cloudflare Workers deployment, not containers) - wrote a standard Node.js Dockerfile (npm install && npm run build && npm run start). Needed two build-environment fixes, neither changing the app's real functionality: (1) the sandbox's TLS-intercepting egress proxy needed NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS pointed at its CA for npm install to succeed at all; (2) switched the base image from node:22-alpine to node:22-bookworm-slim because the Cloudflare Workers runtime (@cloudflare/workerd, invoked unconditionally by next.config.ts's initOpenNextCloudflareForDev() even during a plain build) ships a glibc-only prebuilt binary that doesn't run under Alpine's musl libc; (3) the app's own Google Fonts (next/font/google) build-time fetch isn't reachable from this sandbox - removed the remote Inter import in layout.tsx, which already had a full system-font CSS fallback chain (--font-inter, -apple-system, ... sans-serif), so this only changes the on-screen typeface, not any capability.
